newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Minorco cautions on weak copper price.
newsitem.headline: Minorco cautions on weak copper price.

text.p: Minorco SA said on Thursday that a weaker copper price would impact on second half results, although hedging programmes would provide some protection both in the second half of 1996 and in 1997.
Commenting on prospects in a statement accompanying first-half results, Minorco said industrial commodity prices had shown a marked weakness so far in 1996.
"Although the U.S. economy continues to perform strongly and Europe is showing signs of recovery, Japan remains relatively subdued," the South African-controlled mining group said.
Despite price weakness in the first half, Minorco's expansion programmes and product diversity meant it almost matched the record levels of earnings in the previous period, the company noted.
Net earnings before exceptionals dipped to $200 million in the six months to June 30 from $210 million a year ago, but the bottom line was boosted by a $117 million gain from investment disposals.
"The volume growth achieved in our business during the first half will...partly provide protection against any continuation of commodity price weakeness," Minorco said.
In the medium term, Minorco said the most significant potential lay in major projects now under development.

Collahuasi was the first to commence construction and activities on remaining projects would intensify over the coming months with the development of Cerro Vanguardia in Argentina and Lisheen in Ireland now projected to commence by the end of the year.

Minorco's attributable gold production rose 24 percent in the first half to 340,100 ounces while copper production was up 56 percent to 67,800 tonnes. Zinc and nickel output of 40,700 and 3,300 tonnes respectively were virtually unchanged.
